title: 'Eleven small folios of cypher in numbers' that William Blencowe failed to break (Harley papers)
correspondents: unknown (intercepted letters sent to Blencowe by Robert Harley)
shelfmark: BL Harley/Portland papers (former Loan 29, now Add MS 70001-70523; volume not identified); HMC Portland VIII (1907), pp. 234-235
folio_note: Blencowe to Harley, 22 Jun 1706: 'When these letters came first to my hands, I applied myself diligently to them ... above a month ... Yet I advanced not one step ... forced to quit the work imperfect.' Editor (Lomas): '(There are eleven small folios of cypher in numbers, which are perhaps the letters referred to in the latter part of Blencowe's letter.)'
status: The official decipherer says he could not read them; the editor prints no reading and only guesses the link. The other cipher in the same letter (Bobin's transposition letter to Pellerin) Blencowe read with Bobin's key. known.py on 'Blencowe', 'Bobin', 'Pellerin': Blencowe appears only in other entries (Jaupain intercepts, 1707 Bavarian letter); nothing on these folios. why: A number cipher that defeated Blencowe in 1706, with eleven folios of text: enough for a modern attack.
score_note: Writer and language unknown; Blencowe's failure suggests a large nomenclator or a superencipherment. Length (11 small folios) is good for statistics.
